title: Test a source/build/install/runtime-currentness handoff between VeraMesh and Vera Synology
claim: VeraMesh and Vera Synology expose complementary transport/session versus package/install mechanics, but the first native handoff falsifier found a provenance gap: Synology strongly cross-binds its package to its own exact source manifest, yet the native package identity path does not bind the exact VeraMesh producer repository/head. A reusable handoff therefore remains a missing-contract hypothesis, not an established interchange.
preserved_boundaries: VeraMesh transport authentication, session identity, fencing, path health, mutation ambiguity, and route selection remain VeraMesh-owned.
Synology package metadata, deterministic artifact construction, DSM lifecycle, legacy-state migration, install state, and target-specific readback remain Vera Synology-owned.
A source artifact or manifest cannot imply installed state, current route, live effect, plugin registration, or package activation.
An installed package cannot silently promote stale transport source or older installed bytes into current repository truth.
No device, credential, provider, route, installation, or runtime effect authority is transferred through the interchange.
promotion_evidence: VeraMesh PR #12 exact head 9bffc57930587bf74a12657bbeaa913474ab5574 explicitly separates SOURCE_CREATED, MCP_SERVER_RUNNING, PLUGIN_REGISTERED, CURRENT_ROUTE, READ_PASS, WRITE_PASS, and PROCESS_EXEC_PASS.
VeraMesh mutation-ledger source at the same head separates read-only operations from mutation durability and blocks ambiguous mutation retry without same-session durable idempotency.
Vera Synology PR #3 exact head 553e3a637833c5469f6b99fbc4d597755a0c9a5e contains deterministic SPK verification with artifact/source byte and mode cross-binding against SOURCE_MANIFEST.json.

The Vera Synology stack explicitly records installed operational R6 separately from later R7/current PR source, proving that install/runtime state and source currentness are already distinct concerns.
The source-bound comparison is recorded in experiments/PUBLIC_INTAKE_SECOND_PASS_V1.json.

Experiment VERAMESH_SYNOLOGY_HANDOFF_EXPERIMENT_V1 confirms Synology SOURCE_MANIFEST + verify_spk source can validate local package/source byte, mode, path-set, and closed metadata identity without importing VeraPort session authority.

The same exact native package identity path does not bind the VeraMesh producer repository or exact producer head; Discovery can observe both refs externally, but that is not native Synology package validation.

The proposed neutral record keeps build=NOT_EXECUTED_BY_DISCOVERY, install=NOT_OBSERVED_BY_DISCOVERY, route=NOT_INFERRED, and live_effect=NOT_INFERRED; hostile tests reject promotion of any of those states.
rejection_conditions: The interchange must interpret VeraPort session/authority semantics inside the Synology packaging layer.
The interchange must interpret DSM/package lifecycle semantics inside VeraMesh transport source.
A common currentness record cannot distinguish source identity, build artifact identity, installed artifact identity, runtime route/currentness, and live effect readback.
Adapters or duplicated validation needed for the handoff exceed the current project-local plumbing they would replace.
Either project becomes runtime-dependent on Discovery or on the other repository merely to remain operable.

critical_objections: The projects may already be correctly separated and require only an explicit provenance receipt, not a reusable shared component.
A Discovery-side cross-repo record cannot substitute for a producer binding that the package's own governed validation path can recover and verify.
Adding producer provenance to Synology could become shadow release authority if the field decides acceptability rather than merely binds identity.
Even a safe identity receipt has not yet shown duplicated maintenance reduction or a second independent consumer.

notes: Candidate generated from the 2026-09-21 second-pass public intake.
No merge, install, route, provider, credential, or runtime action follows.
First native handoff experiment failed the stronger end-to-end claim: current Synology validation proves local package/source identity but not the exact VeraMesh producer binding.

Next valid experiment: specify a non-authoritative producer-provenance receipt that binds exact producer source identity but cannot promote build/install/route/effect state; do not modify VeraMesh or Vera Synology without their owning lane/authority.
